label: t/z/g/y input at original position 2-3, boosted by earlier v/m
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase at t=2 or 3 (99% of mass; never in the copy phase, rarely at the delimiter, t=1 or t=4). The current input token matters most: t (8.9x lift), z, g, y; e and c much more weakly. It fires on the first occurrence of that token in the sequence. The tokens just before it set the magnitude: v and m earlier in the prefix (prev_tok m/v, first_tok v) give the largest activations, e.g. v v v [t], a v m [t], n v m [z]. h, i, d, n, l and f give moderate boosts. The same t/z/g/y token at t=2-3 after other prefixes is often inactive, which limits precision. It acts like a combined current-token plus prefix-token selectivity, not a clean boolean rule. The simpler rule t in {2,3} & in_tok in {t,z,g,y} & first occurrence scores dev F1 0.50 with mass recall 0.82. Adding the prefix-set condition gives dev F1 0.58 with mass recall 0.75.
